title: Class Capacity Truth
user: Small language schools and tutoring centres running paid group assessments or classes who need the capacity shown to families to match real seats. Paying customer: school operations lead; wedge: trustworthy seat inventory and waitlist conversion at $99/month.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The scheduling discussion identifies group bookings and reminders as paid add-ons and says generic scheduling products are rigid, impersonal, and overkill for small businesses.
An English language school reports Cal.com showing only one or two places available while all places remained available, explicitly tying the defect to booking more level checks.

recurrence: The same class-booking problem appears as both a small-business product complaint and a school operator's revenue-impacting seat-count defect.
current_workaround: Keep a spreadsheet alongside a booking tool, manually confirm every group booking, and call waitlisted families one at a time.
incumbents_and_gap: Calendly and Cal.com offer group events; full school-information systems are broad and costly. Neither is a lightweight capacity truth layer that reconciles seats, blocks oversell, and converts a waitlist for small schools.
smallest_useful_product: Connect one calendar, define class capacity and cutoff rules, expose a parent booking page, reconcile bookings every few minutes, and send one-click released-seat offers. Non-goals: student records, grading, or a full SIS.
success_measure: A pilot has zero incorrect seat displays for 90 days and fills at least 25% of released places from its waitlist within 24 hours.
monetization: subscription — $99/month per school is small relative to one filled assessment group and supports monitoring and notifications.
constraints: Protect child and parent data, minimize data retention, provide role-based access, and support regional privacy requirements.
why_distinct: It is a narrow capacity-reconciliation and waitlist revenue product, not another school management suite.
